verdict.rationale: YYLO is a command-line orchestrator for coding agents, so configurable autonomy or permission tiers are a fair question for it. The evidence documents nothing like tiered autonomy levels or approval gates that control what an agent may do without manual confirmation. The nearest items are adjacent and earn no credit: Simple/Advanced workspace topologies, a read-only preflight, explicit merge boundaries, and a prompt telling the agent not to edit files.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can set tiered autonomy levels controlling what an agent can do without manual confirmation
